ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: PRC: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (2024 revision, effective 1 Jan. 2025); Counter-Terrorism Law of the People's Republic of China (2018 amendment); Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information (PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3 [2024], effective 1 Nov. 2024); Measures for Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Financing of Terrorism Customer Due Diligence and Customer Identity Information and Transaction Records Preservation (PBOC Order [2022] No. 1, effective 1 Mar. 2022); Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 revision, effective 1 July 2024); Administrative Provisions on Enterprise Name Registration (2021 revision); Regulations on the Registration Administration of Market Subjects (2021). mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Company Registration Record) of the Taiwanese investing shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Cross-Strait consular legalization channel; Hague Apostille is not applicable. Sequence: Taiwan notary authentication of the MOEA certificate -> Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) verification -> Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS) verification -> submission to local SAMR. Do not add a Hague apostille on the same instrument.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (or equivalent current Company Registration Note) of the Taiwanese shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan; commercial registration department
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Non-Hague path; Taiwan notary -> SEF -> ARATS -> SAMR / local foreign-investment registry. These steps are consular legalization equivalents and are mutually exclusive with apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney authorizing execution of the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture incorporation documents and UBO declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the Taiwanese investing company; notarized by Taiwan civil notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan civil notary notarial certification -> SEF verification -> ARATS verification -> recipient Chinese notary/public security/registry. No apostille because Taiwan is not an Apostille Convention party under the PRC legal order.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (and latest Amendments) of the Taiwanese investing shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan, as registered; shareholder meeting or board for certified true copy
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Cross-strait consular legalization: Taiwan notary -> SEF -> ARATS -> SAMR. Apostille not applicable; do not chain with Hague certification.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter / banker's confirmation of account conduct for the Taiwanese shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan-based commercial bank holding the investor's TWD corporate account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank signatory's signature authenticated by Taiwan notary and, if the receiving Chinese bank or tax bureau requires, SEF/ARATS verification; otherwise direct bank-to-bank telex/email confirmation. Never apostilled; consular legalization equivalent only if demanded.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before signing the JV agreement and again at closing, all UBOs, directors, senior managers, authorized signatories, and commercial counterparties (including photographers/AI asset suppliers and Stripe/PayPal merchants) must be screened against (i) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list and 1267/1988 designations, (ii) US OFAC SDN List and 50% Rule consolidated sanctions, (iii) UK HMT consolidated list, (iv) EU restrictive measures, (v) PRC lists of designated terrorists and money launders, (vi) PBOC/SAMR beneficial owner register annotations, (vii) Taiwan FIU suspicious activity reports, and (viii) Interpol and negative news. PEP status must be determined using the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) 2023 recommendations: treat foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs and international-organization PEPs as higher risk; perform enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth/source-of-funds verification, family/close associate checks, and obtain senior-management approval before onboarding; repeat screening every 90 days for as long as the JV is active and immediately upon any trigger event. Screening results must be documented in an audit trail retained for at least 5 years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) Enterprise Name Self-Service Reservation System, National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS), and the local municipal market-regulation one-stop online platform
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the PRC Enterprise Name Registration Administration Provisions, a qualified Chinese name must consist of four tiers: (1) administrative division (e.g., city/district); (2) distinctive enterprise name (字号) consisting of two or more simplified Chinese characters; (3) industry or business-characteristics expression; (4) statutory organizational form (e.g., Limited Liability Company / Co., Ltd.). The registered name must be in simplified Chinese. A foreign-invested JV may apply a separate English name for bank and trademark use, but only the Chinese name is registered; the investor's non-Chinese name must be transliterated phonetically into simplified Chinese in the distinctive-name tier if used as the brand. Taiwanese investor names are generally rendered in Traditional Chinese first and simplified Chinese on the Chinese registered name; no Latin-only registered names are permitted.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon receiving a name-rejection decision, the applicant must within 60 days file an administrative reconsideration request with the municipal market-regulation administration or the local people's government at the same level, or institute an administrative lawsuit within six months. The written request must state the exact grounds, the proposed Chinese name, the four-tier structure, evidence of the reserved/or invalidated name, and a comparison chart with any conflicting registered name. If time-critical, ask for urgent processing; attach a power of attorney and notarized corporate resolutions. The reconsideration organ must decide within 60 days, extendable by 30 days for complex cases.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office and commercial mailbox addresses are rejected, not merely disfavored, by Chinese municipal tax bureaus and banks for this industry. A Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture engaged in stock photography/AI visual asset marketplace must have a real, dedicated office with the entity name displayed, because: (1) SAMR rejects registered addresses lacking property-use rights or lease registrations; (2) tax authorities require a place of business for invoice issuance, VAT registration, and permanent-establishment economic substance; (3) commercial banks require branch site visits before RMB/foreign currency account opening; and (4) SAFE will not approve foreign exchange registration for a company with a letterbox address. A shared licensed co-working space can pass only if there is a dedicated desk, mailbox, meeting-room allocation, and management or staff presence during business hours; a pure virtual office with no personnel will be rejected.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Act of Taiwan (R.O.C.), as amended, Articles 6, 129, 133, 145, 148, 156, 161, 171, 172, 192, 216, 387 and 392; read together with the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, Articles 6, 7 and 8, for the foreign-invested equity joint venture approval and capital remittance requirements.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan; One-Stop Company Registration Online Service; Investment Commission, MOEA for foreign investment approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Registration Application Form (Establishment Registration) together with the Articles of Incorporation and the Capital Verification Report.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed for a service company classified under ISIC 7420 under the Taiwan Company Act. However, the Company must maintain paid-up capital sufficient for its intended business scope, and foreign shareholders must obtain Investment Commission approval and remit their subscription in convertible foreign exchange into Taiwan. Funds must be deposited into a temporary bank account in the Company's name and verified by a Taiwan-licensed certified public accountant before filing; no blocked escrow account is required after registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF CN_JV_LTD, formerly the CN_JV_LTD Establishment Committee, a company limited by shares to be incorporated under the Taiwan Company Act. The first Board of Directors meeting was duly convened on [Date] at [Place], with all directors present and with notice waived by unanimous consent. After due deliberation, the following resolutions were adopted by unanimous vote. 1. ARTICLES OF INCORPORATION: The Board confirmed and adopted the Articles of Incorporation as the Company's constitution and directed that they be filed with the Ministry of Economic Affairs. 2. ESTABLISHMENT CONFIRMATION: The Board acknowledged the incorporation date to be the date of the MOEA establishment registration certificate and accepted the unified business number assigned by the competent authority. 3. SHARE CAPITAL AND SUBSCRIPTIONS: The Board confirmed that the authorized share capital is [NT$ amount], divided into [number] ordinary shares of par value NT$10 each, of which [number] shares, total NT$ [amount], have been subscribed and fully paid up by the founding shareholders. The Board approved the share allocation schedule contained in the subscription ledger, accepted each subscription, ordered the issue of share certificates, and directed the Company Secretary to register the shareholders in the share register. 4. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Board designated [Bank Name], [Branch], Taiwan, as the principal banker and authorized the opening of operating and foreign currency accounts in the Company name. The Chairperson, General Manager, and Company Secretary are hereby appointed account signatories; any two signatories shall co-sign cheques and payment instructions above the approval threshold, and the common corporate seal shall be kept by the Company Secretary under joint supervision. 5. REGISTERED OFFICE: The Board adopted [Address], Taiwan, as the Company's registered office and legal service address. The General Manager and Company Secretary were authorized to execute any lease, utility, nameplate, and registration documents for the registered office with all applicable authorities. 6. OFFICER AND SUPERVISOR APPOINTMENTS: The Board appointed [Name] as Chairperson and Managing Director, [Name] as General Manager, [Name] as Company Secretary, [Name] as Accounting Officer, and [Name] as Supervisor, each to serve until the next annual general meeting. The Chairperson shall preside, the General Manager shall conduct the business of the Company, the Company Secretary shall maintain corporate records, statutory filings, minutes, and share registers, the Accounting Officer shall maintain true and fair books of account, and the Supervisor shall independently audit the Company's accounts and report to shareholders. 7. ACCOUNTING PERIOD AND AUDITOR: The Board adopted the financial year beginning January 1 and ending December 31 and appointed [CPA Firm] as independent certified public accountant to audit the annual financial statements and tax reports. 8. IMPLEMENTATION: The Chairperson, General Manager, and Company Secretary, acting jointly in pairs, are authorized to execute, notarize, file, and deliver all registration forms, declarations, bank mandates, and government filings required to complete incorporation and to operate lawfully in Taiwan. This resolution was unanimously adopted and is effective immediately. Passed on [Date] at [Place].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Foreign Investment Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) One-Stop Company Registration Online Portal; Investment Commission, MOEA for foreign investment approval.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a company name pre-approval application through the MOEA One-Stop Company Registration portal using the proposed English and Chinese business names. The chosen names must not conflict with registered companies, trademark rights, or prohibited terms. Simultaneously, if any shareholder is a non-Taiwan resident or foreign entity, file an investment application with the Investment Commission, MOEA under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, disclosing the ultimate beneficial owner, investment amount, business scope classified under ISIC 7420, and source of funds. Execute and notarize the Articles of Incorporation before a notary public so they are ready for subsequent filing. Obtain the name pre-approval certificate and the Foreign Investment Approval Letter before proceeding.
required_dossiers: Proposed English and Chinese company names
Passport or corporate identification of each shareholder
Evidence of authorized representative for corporate shareholders
Power of attorney to local agent if appointed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Within the prescribed period, normally 14 days after receiving a rejection or correction notice, file a supplementary response through the same portal. For name conflicts, submit a revised name. For Investment Commission queries, provide bank provenance, UBO declarations, or a revised investment plan. If the authority formally refuses, request an administrative reconsideration or appeal within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Deposit, CPA Verification and Pre-Registration Document Execution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized domestic bank in Taiwan; Taiwan-licensed certified public accountant; Notary Public where Articles of Incorporation require notarization.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After foreign investment approval is obtained, open a temporary capital account in the Company's intended name at an authorized bank and remit the subscribed paid-up capital from overseas. Obtain the Foreign Exchange Inward Remittance Certificate and the bank balance certificate. Appoint a Taiwan-licensed certified public accountant to perform capital verification, to review the remittance certificate and bank statements, and to issue a Capital Verification Report certifying that the paid-up capital has been fully received. Prepare and sign the final Articles of Incorporation, director and supervisor consent forms, and registered office lease or use consent. Ensure all signatures match the identity documents presented to the notary public and to the bank.
required_dossiers: Consent letters of directors and supervisor
Registered office lease or consent letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or CPA flags missing capital, insufficient remittance, or signature mismatches, correct the remittance documentation or pass a shareholder resolution adjusting the capital amount. Reissue the CPA report and resubmit all corrected documents before proceeding to MOEA filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan; One-Stop Company Registration Online Service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation application with MOEA within the statutory period after the Articles of Incorporation are signed. Use the One-Stop Company Registration portal or a municipal authorized registration window. Submit the Company Registration Application Form, Articles of Incorporation, name pre-approval certificate, capital verification report, registered office consent, director and supervisor identification, company seal card, and all required declarations. Pay the state filing fee and obtain the official receipt. Once approved, MOEA will issue the company establishment registration certificate and the unified business number, and the Company will acquire separate legal personality as of the registration date. Verify every item on the registration certificate against the final Articles before accepting delivery.
required_dossiers: Notarized or signed Articles of Incorporation
Registered office lease or consent letter
Consent and identification of directors, supervisor and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOEA issues an inquiry or suspension, file a formal response with corrected documents within 15 days of notice. Pay any surcharge if the delay is caused by the Company. If the defect is substantive, pass a board or shareholder resolution to amend the Articles and refile with a covering letter requesting preservation of the original filing date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Unified Business Number Activation and Post-Registration Administrative Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance, Taiwan; Bureau of Labor Insurance; National Health Insurance Administration; authorized commercial bank branch for account activation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within the statutory period after company establishment, register with the National Taxation Bureau for profit-seeking enterprise income tax and value-added or business tax, and apply for the unified invoice registration. The Company seal and responsible person seal must be filed with the tax authority. Register employees with the Bureau of Labor Insurance and National Health Insurance program. Activate the corporate operating accounts at the designated bank using the MOEA company establishment registration certificate, the board resolution authorizing signatories, and the company seal card. Confirm the electronic filing credentials with the Ministry of Finance and set up accounting books denominated in New Taiwan Dollars. Complete any subsequent central bank foreign exchange filings required for future outward remittances of capital and dividends.
required_dossiers: Company seal and responsible person seal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is rejected because company registration data is missing, obtain a certified copy of the MOEA registration record and present it to the National Taxation Bureau. If invoice registration is delayed, request urgent express processing. If labor insurance or health insurance data is incomplete, correct the employee roster and refile. If the bank questions the board resolution, obtain a board meeting minutes extract with original seals and resubmit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable — the entity conducts no ISIC 1xxx/2xxx/3xxx/4xxx/52xx manufacturing, chemical, assembly, warehousing, or physical logistics operations; it operates a digital stock media and generative AI visual asset marketplace.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Administration (EPA), Executive Yuan, Taiwan (R.O.C.)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable (Exempt) — no environmental impact assessment registration or full EIA report required because the project is a pure digital service with no physical construction, manufacturing, or waste-generating industrial process.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable — zero industrial wastewater discharges, zero regulated VOC emissions, zero hazardous waste generation; office operations generate only municipal waste and small ICT e-waste that must be handled under municipal collection and Taiwan WEEE take-back rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable — no civil defense industrial permit, factory-use fire safety certificate, structural load inspection, or occupational health clearance is required. If a general commercial office is leased, the building must comply with the Taiwan Fire Services Act and the municipal building code, and the lessor must provide a lawful use license and, where triggered, a fire safety inspection certificate.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, National Taxation Administration, Taiwan; online electronic tax portal: https://etax.nat.gov.tw; e-invoice clearance and registration portal: https://einvoice.nat.gov.tw
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Obtain investment approval from the Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan, under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals. Step 2: Complete company registration under the Company Act with the Ministry of Economic Affairs, establishing the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture as a Taiwanese limited company; obtain the official company registration approval/record. Step 3: Before commencing business, file the statutory Business Tax registration application with the local branch office of the National Taxation Administration, attaching the company registration record, articles of incorporation, board resolution, foreign investment approval, responsible person identification and proof of a bank account maintained in Taiwan. Step 4: The National Taxation Administration will assign the statutory eight-digit Taxpayer Uniform Number (UBN), which is the unified Tax Identification Number and VAT/Business Tax registration number. Step 5: Register simultaneously as a Uniform Invoice issuer and e-invoice taxpayer, and complete withholding-tax registration for salaries and other domestic-source payments. Step 6: File all subsequent periodic Business Tax and income tax returns under that UBN and notify the tax authority of any changes to business status, address or legal representation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Taiwan does not provide check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections; the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture is mandatorily taxed as a separate entity-level taxpayer.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taiwan Business Tax under the Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary threshold for tax registration: any person or entity carrying on taxable business in Taiwan must apply for tax registration with the National Taxation Administration before commencing operations. The NT$200,000 per month figure is the rate-and-invoicing boundary: small-scale businesses with monthly taxable sales at or below NT$200,000 may be assessed at the simplified 1% Business Tax rate, while regular taxpayers with monthly taxable sales exceeding NT$200,000 must issue Uniform Invoices and account for the standard 5% VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan operates a mandatory Uniform Invoice system administered by the Ministry of Finance. Regular VAT taxpayers and businesses above the NT$200,000 monthly sales boundary must issue Uniform Invoices for every taxable sale. Under the E-Invoice mandate, the taxpayer must connect to the Ministry of Finance E-Invoice Integrated Service Platform using the statutory Turnkey/API interface; each invoice is issued with a ministerial invoice number, random check code and QR code, and the invoice data is transmitted to the platform within the prescribed filing window for tax-authority validation, discrepancy matching and anti-fraud control. There is no separate physical fiscal stamp; the electronic record in the Ministry of Finance platform is the fiscal clearance evidence.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 7 of the Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act, a 0% Business Tax rate is available for goods exported out of Taiwan and for services provided by a Taiwan business to a non-Taiwan customer where the service is delivered for use or consumption entirely outside Taiwan. For the ISIC 7420 stock-photo/generative visual assets activity, the taxpayer must prove that the purchaser is non-resident, the licensed digital assets are delivered offshore by electronic transfer or download, the consideration is payable in foreign exchange, and the foreign exchange receipt is timely repatriated. The zero-rating also makes input VAT attributable to the export sale refundable.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, being the official export declaration filed via the Ministry of Finance Customs Administration online clearance system for physical exported goods.
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill covering the export shipment where physical media or goods are moved to the overseas customer.
Inward Remittance Certificate or Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate issued by an Authorized Foreign Exchange Bank, evidencing receipt and repatriation of the overseas customer payment.
Executed international sales contract, license agreement or purchase order naming the offshore customer and specifying the exact license fee/value.
Zero-rated Uniform Invoice issued to the foreign purchaser with the statutory zero-rate tax code.
Digital delivery evidence for stock photos or generative visual assets, including download logs, usage reports, IP address records and platform reports showing delivery to a non-Taiwan customer.
Attribution record matching the export sales consideration to the corresponding input tax credits claimed.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Taiwan tax authorities audit zero-rating claims by cross-checking the Customs export declaration, transport documents, Uniform Invoice data and the Authorized Foreign Exchange Bank remittance ledger. If the taxpayer cannot substantiate a genuine offshore customer, offshore delivery/use, or receipt and repatriation of export proceeds within the statutory period (normally 180 days), the supply is recharacterized as domestic taxable and assessed at the standard 5% VAT, with interest and penalties. Under the Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act, false zero-rating, issuance of false Uniform Invoices or intentional understatement of taxable sales attracts a penalty of five to eight times the tax evaded, suspension of business, and criminal referral for tax fraud where fraudulent documentation is shown. Any previously allowed zero-rating or input-tax refund can be clawed back retrospectively if the supporting customs, transport, contract, digital-delivery or foreign-exchange documents are found to be fabricated, incomplete or not verified in audit.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) (CBC), with the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) and the Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA-IC) as co-regulators for foreign investment and banking compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Taiwan maintains a managed floating exchange-rate regime administered by the Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) (CBC). The New Taiwan Dollar (TWD) is effectively convertible for current-account transactions, including trade settlements, service fees, royalties, dividends, and branch remittances, provided the underlying business documentation and a foreign-exchange declaration are submitted through a CBC-designated bank. Capital-account flows, especially an inbound equity injection into a Taiwan JV from mainland China, are not automatically convertible: the investment must first receive authorization from the Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs and the remittance must be released under a specific CBC transaction code after bank compliance review. Export proceeds no longer bear a mandatory surrender ratio; they can be held in Foreign Currency Deposit accounts or converted at market rates. Dividend and profit remittances to non-resident shareholders require audited financial statements, tax clearance, and withholding tax receipts. The CBC retains emergency powers to impose limits, require advance approval for large transactions, and direct designated banks to collect additional declarations, so full balance-of-payments data visibility is a structural reality.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds are subject to repatriation rather than surrender: the exporter must bring the foreign-currency receivables into Taiwan through a CBC-designated bank by the contracted payment maturity or, for open-account export bills, within 180 days of the export shipment date unless an extension has been approved by the CBC. The mandatory conversion ratio is effectively zero; the exporter may retain 100% of the proceeds in a Foreign Currency Deposit (FCD) account or convert any portion to TWD at the prevailing bank counter rate. The CBC foreign-exchange declaration must be filed for each receipt through the bank's reporting platform, with the export declaration, commercial invoice, bill of lading, and tax invoice attached. Failure to repatriate or declare on time subjects the JV to a written rectification order, administrative fines, and potential downgrade of the bank's internal KYC rating.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low. Taiwanese law reserves the taking of deposits, execution of foreign-exchange transactions, and operation of domestic clearing membership to licensed banks and CBC-authorized designated banks; a foreign fintech EMI such as Wise, Revolut, or Airwallex does not hold a Taiwan bank license and cannot clear NTD through the CBC interbank settlement system or perform the statutory capital-verification and foreign-exchange declaration duties required for an inbound equity JV. Stripe and PayPal are permissible only as merchant and payment-service-provider collection tools for e-commerce or licensing revenue, and every settled amount must flow onward to a Taiwan commercial bank account for treasury concentration. An EMI account may be used for sublimit operational expenses in a non-core jurisdiction, but it cannot substitute for the Taiwan resident bank relationship, and the FSC will treat the JV as unbanked if it relies solely on an EMI.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory in-branch: Yes. FSC enforcement guidance and CBC AML KYC practices require at least one statutory director, or a validly authorized director with a power of attorney, to appear physically at the opening branch and complete the compliance interview with a bank AML officer before account activation. Remote consular proxy or video-only opening is generally not accepted for a newly formed foreign-invested entity whose UBO is a mainland Chinese party, because the bank must conduct enhanced due diligence and verify execution capacity in person. A supplemental signatory may be appointed by notarized power of attorney; physical presence of the general manager or CFO is recommended when the statutory director is non-resident. Where the director cannot travel, the bank may, under its institutional risk appetite, accept a personal visit by a notarized and legalized proxy only after the statutory director undergoes a remote video interview and legal counsel issues an opinion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mainland Chinese corporate parent appears in the UBO chain, creating heightened cross-strait funds-sourcing, sanction, and politically exposed person (PEP) review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and legalized certificate of incorporation and articles of association of the mainland Chinese parent; audited financial statements for the last three years; tax residence and business registration; extract from the mainland China corporate information database; UBO registration declaration signed by all shareholders; clean sanction and PEP screening reports from a commercial data vendor; sworn funding-source statement; and shareholder resolution approving the Taiwan JV equity injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound equity capital from mainland China could be deemed illegal cross-strait round-tripping or unapproved foreign direct investment without a valid outward investment permit.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: MOEA-IC Taiwan JV approval certificate; PRC SAFE ODI or FDI registration filing receipt; NDRC and MOFCOM outbound investment records where applicable; original SWIFT MT103 with PRC bank FX purpose code; CBC foreign-exchange declaration completed at the Taiwan receiving bank; legal opinion from China-qualified counsel confirming the outbound remittance is lawful; capital injection schedule; and CPA capital verification report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The digital stock-photo and AI business model has high intellectual-property royalty flows and low physical assets, which banks may profile as layering, money laundering, or undisclosed beneficial ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: IP assignment agreements and title chain; copyright registrations in relevant markets; photographer and AI content supplier contracts; payout ledger with tax withholding certificates; platform sales reports and Stripe or PayPal reconciliation; board-approved transfer pricing policy for royalties; legal opinion confirming genuine commercial operations; and a public catalogue of the stock-photo marketplace.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The JV lacks a substantive local operating presence, payroll, or verifiable location, raising shell-company red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered office lease or property ownership certificate in Taiwan; utility bills and business premises photographs; corporate seal and statutory director registration; monthly payroll and Taiwan labor insurance records; local bookkeeping or accounting firm appointment letter; Taiwan National Taxation Bureau return filings; and a written consent for the bank to conduct a physical office visit.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity capital must arrive via the international banking network as a SWIFT MT103, or as a Fedwire or CHIPS wire in USD, to the JV designated Capital Escrow Account at a CBC-authorized designated commercial bank. The wire reference line must show the MOEA-IC approval number and a clear purpose code of Inward Remittance for Direct Investment rather than a trade-goods code. The remitting bank, being the mainland Chinese parent bank, must use the PRC SAFE-approved ODI remittance purpose code and attach a copy of the foreign-exchange registration certificate. Upon receipt, the Taiwan bank notifies the CBC through the FX declaration system, conducts source-of-funds verification, and credits a restricted capital-verification account; the JV CPA then verifies paid-in capital and issues a capital verification report before funds can be moved to an operating account. The capital escrow account may be used for approved business expenses, land, buildings, equipment, working capital, and IP license fees only after MOEA-IC and CBC post-approval milestones are satisfied.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound treasury disbursements are cleared through three principal rails: ordinary operating and royalty payments are sent by SWIFT MT103 from the Taiwan JV Foreign Currency Deposit account, with CBC declaration purpose code for Royalties and License Fees or Services, supported by the governing license agreement, invoice, withholding tax declaration, and bank payment instruction; large procurement of hardware or software for the AI stock-photo infrastructure is settled by commercial irrevocable letter of credit issued by the Taiwan corporate bank and advised through the beneficiary bank, with the full set of shipping and acceptance documents; smaller open-account transactions use documentary collections, either documents against payment or documents against acceptance, where the Taiwan bank forwards shipping or title documents against payment or acceptance. For RMB-settled trade with mainland China counterparties, the CNY leg must clear via the Bank of China Taipei Branch, the Taiwan-designated RMB clearing bank, under the CBC and PBOC cross-strait clearing agreement. All instructions must be signed under dual authorization and reconciled daily.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore USD/TWD forward foreign exchange contracts with CBC-licensed designated banks, limited to contracted royalty, import, export, and equity-related cash flow exposures, with maturities up to 18 months and no speculative leverage beyond 100% of underlying cash-flow documentation.

Cross-currency swaps in USD/TWD and RMB/TWD for converting offshore operating receipts or financing into the JV functional currency when the underlying has a verifiable direct investment or trade basis, with board approval and CBC reporting through the designated bank.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards on TWD are not permitted for resident corporate entities in Taiwan; non-resident investors may execute NDFs through a CBC-authorized branch only when the notional corresponds to actual TWD exposure and the proceeds are settled offshore, avoiding prohibited speculative offshore NTD trading.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements, business report, and shareholders' approval minutes filed with company registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year end (for calendar year, by June 30)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing: administrative fine of NTD 10,000–50,000 for each violation plus continued per-month penalty; responsible person may be compelled to file by MOEA

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Regular shareholders' meeting approving annual financial statements and distribution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders; MOEA registration if meeting resolution changes articles or capital
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year end (for calendar year, by June 30)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene: competent authority may summon shareholders; responsible person subject to administrative fine up to NTD 200,000 and continued fines

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return and undistributed surplus tax filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after fiscal year end (for calendar year, by May 31)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Understood: additional tax 3% per month up to 30% of underreported tax plus late interest; tax evasion triggers criminal liability and enhanced penalties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Report of directors, managers, and shareholders holding >10% (UBO/controllers report) if any change occurred
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs central registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after any share transfer or management change; no annual filing if no change occurs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or updating incomplete data: NTD 50,000–500,000 administrative fine plus order to rectify; continued noncompliance accrues daily penalty up to NTD 50,000

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory CPA audit if paid-in capital ≥ NTD 30 million or annual net revenue ≥ NTD 50 million; below thresholds financial statements may be internally prepared but must comply with Business Entity Accounting Act standards
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan Enterprise Accounting Standards (EAS) for non-public SMEs, with optional application of International Financial Reporting Standards (Taiwan-IFRS) for large non-public companies; books kept under Business Entity Accounting Act

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan does not require an annual UBO confirmation filing; Article 22-1 Company Act mandates a one-time report within 15 days of establishment and an updated report within 15 days of any event affecting directors, managers, or shareholding above 10%. The holding company must verify share-transfer data and re-silence a no-change annual statement only if such a change occurs, and must retain underlying ownership records for at least 7 years.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 – USD 8,000 for a low-risk stock media entity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 20% on net taxable income exceeding NT$120,000 for fiscal years beginning on or after 1 January 2018; retained earnings not distributed within 3 years attract an additional 5% retained earnings surcharge.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D and innovation tax credits under the Statute for Industrial Innovation; net-operating-loss deduction under the Income Tax Act with a 10-year carryforward; 10-year tax holiday for qualifying new green energy and digital asset production investments; 5% retained earnings surcharge coordinate with the 20% rate yields an aggregate economic rate of 24.5% on distributed residual profits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return (Form 40) and detailed schedules; e-filing mandatory via the Ministry of Finance 'CPB Money' electronic tax filing platform (Web: tax.nat.gov.tw) using the company's TW-certificate and FinTech token.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; separately, quarterly provisional tax installments are required for enterprises with annual turnover exceeding NT$50 million or for entities that have prior-year taxable income above NT$200 million.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Calendar-year enterprises must file by 31 May of the following taxable year; for fiscal-year-end other than December 31, the return must be filed no later than 4 months after the fiscal year-end. Provisional installments are due in September and December each year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross sales, service fees, licensing fees, royalty income, commissions, and other operating revenue derived from the stock photography and AI visual asset platform, reported on an accrual basis net of returns and allowances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident branch or taxable permanent establishment reports Taiwan-sourced income only; foreign revenue not effectively connected with Taiwan operations is excluded unless attributable to a Taiwanese PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 05: Cost of Goods and Services
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct production costs, content acquisition costs, AI inference model licensing costs, server hosting, royalty payments to independent photographers/stock contributors, and digital fulfillment costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident taxpayers may deduct only expenses reasonably allocated to Taiwan-source gross income under the direct allocation method; transfer pricing adjustments under Articles 43-1 and 43-3 apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sales, administrative, payroll, marketing, legal, and technology expenses, including platform infrastructure and data security costs; depreciation on AI processing equipment and intangible amortization.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Headquarters overhead allocations to a Taiwanese PE must be evidenced by documented cost allocation tables and must not exceed arm's length recoverable costs; unsubstantiated expenses are disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciling statutory net income with tax-basis taxable income; additions for retained earnings surcharge, non-deductible penalties, undocumented related-party expenses, and excluded tax-exempt dividends.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any adjustment to Taiwan-source profit from deemed remittances of royalties or fungible intra-group AI asset transfers must be reported as a separate reconciliation memorandum.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 99/100: Income Tax Liability and Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax at 20% on taxable income, reduced by: foreign income tax credit for Taiwan-source profits taxed abroad, unrecaptured investment credits, and qualifying digital platform incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident branch tax, rather than dividend withholding, is applied if the Taiwan entity constitutes a fixed place of business; Article 25 taxation on deemed assessed profits (1% of gross business revenue for certain technology and platform services) is available only upon approval.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a surcharge of 1% of the unassessed tax amount for each two-week period, up to 15%, plus interest at the postal savings two-year fixed-deposit rate, unless notice has been issued. If the tax administrator assesses a return after failure to respond to a notice, an additional 20% of the assessed tax is imposed, and the responsible person may also be subject to criminal prosecution for intentional non-compliance.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% on dividends distributed to non-resident enterprise shareholders; 21% applies to distributions from earnings subject to the 5% retained earnings surtax. No further withholding or enterprise income tax applies to the remainder because the Taiwan company has already borne full corporate income tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a Double Taxation Agreement (DTA) reduction on dividends, the non-resident investor must: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the tax authority of the residence jurisdiction; (2) file Form 28 (Application for Treaty Rate Withholding or Business Profits Exemption) with the Taiwan National Taxation Bureau before the dividend distribution date; (3) submit a beneficial ownership declaration and proof that the shareholder meets the treaty's minimum holding period (usually 1 year and not less than 25% shareholding); (4) upon approval, the payer applies the reduced DTA rate (typically 5%–10%) at source. If the application is not approved before payment, the surplus withholding must be reclaimed through an amended return within 5 years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: In the absence of a treaty, royalty payments to non-resident enterprises are subject to 20% withholding, and interest paid to non-resident enterprises is subject to 20% withholding. Under many Taiwan DTAs, royalties are reduced to 10%–15% and interest to 10%. Payments made to communication, digital content, or software patent pools may be recharacterized as income from Taiwan-source royalties under Article 8, requiring the payer to withhold at 20% unless a treaty or Article 25 deemed-profit election applies.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File documenting related-party transactions is mandatory if annual related-party purchases, sales, royalty, interest, or other monetary transactions exceed NT$50 million in aggregate. A Master File is required for multinational groups that report consolidated group revenue above NT$30 billion or when a Taiwan entity closes related-party transactional volume above NT$200 million. Country-by-country reporting applies to ultimate parent groups with consolidated revenue over NT$30 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR); however, tax authority audits apply the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) under Article 12-1 of the Income Tax Act and the substance-over-form doctrine. A Taiwan company licensing AI-generated stock imagery through structures lacking a local de facto operational core — no local managers, no servers or data preprocessing infrastructure, no local contract negotiation capacity, and no payroll substance — is highly vulnerable to recharacterization as a conduit entity. Application of Article 43-4 (controlled foreign corporation rules) will impute undistributed profits to Taiwanese resident shareholders if the company has low substance and avoids dividend distributions for over 3 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating Taiwan-sourced subscription or stock-photo licensing revenue; recording fictitious content-acquisition payments to overseas shell photographers; overstating AI infrastructure costs; or creating artificial net losses to avoid the statutory 20% corporate tax and to claim a 10-year loss carryforward.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 110 of the Income Tax Act, the taxpayer is liable for a surcharge of up to 3 times the underpaid tax amount; with intentional bookkeeping fraud, under Article 43 of the Tax Collection Act, criminal fines and confiscation of avoided profit may apply. False invoicing costs an additional 5%–10% penalty under the Uniform Invoice Violation Penalty Guidelines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign fraudulent tax returns or authorize misreporting are jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate tax plus penalties. The Taiwan tax court may impose civil restitution; prosecutors may apply a travel ban under the Bail Law when tax evasion exceeds NT$2 million, and imprisonment of up to 5 years plus a personal tax penalty is possible. The corporate veil will be pierced where the director used the JV as a mere alteration ego to shield overseas revenue.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the CN_TW_CN_JV_LTD as a tax-driven shell: minimal Taiwan employees, no Taiwan office, remote control from mainland China or third-country jurisdiction, centralized booking of AI-generated stock royalties in a low-tax intermediary, and using circular investments with no genuine business purpose.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The National Taxation Bureau will recharacterize transactions under the GAAR, imposing 20% tax on deemed Taiwan-source income, adding a 1.5x surcharge on unpaid tax, and denying carryforwards. In addition, the Commercial Registration Authority may revoke the company's registration if the 'limited purpose' of the legal entity cannot support the business scope under the Company Act; this triggers automatic tax collection within 30 days.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under the Company Act Article 23, directors who cause the company to conduct a fictitious commercial design are liable to creditors for full repayment. A director may be held criminally liable for false financial disclosure and imprisoned for up to 3 years. Escaping China/Taiwan may be prevented by travel restraints; joint asset freezes are routinely issued by the Taipei District Court on application by the National Taxation Bureau.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Cross-border payments through Stripe and PayPal settled into offshore PSP or nominee merchant accounts, using obfuscated payment chains without clear identify verification (KYC) of stock photo contributors, or receiving royalty payments that public digital media credential evidence shows as unauthorized or commercially implausible.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Money Laundering Control Act imposes criminal liability on legal persons and responsible individuals: fines up to NT$10 million, and imprisonment of up to 7 years for intentional laundering. The Financial Supervisory Commission may impose a banking ban and freeze the company's payment rails; Stripe and PayPal have contractual termination clauses that mirror FATF list sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly structure trade through interposed shell entities to conceal beneficial ownership face personal seizure of Taiwan financial assets and real estate. The Supreme Court has upheld civil piercing where corporate formalities are ignored for AML avoidance; the director may also be barred from serving as manager within the financial sector under the Securities and Exchange Act. A travel ban is automatically considered by the prosecutor if the amount exceeds NT$15 million and the defendant has residences abroad.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to maintain the local file/master file when related-party cross-border royalties (AI content licensing from mainland Chinese group companies), content production fees, or tech service charges exceed the NT$50 million threshold; or applying a one-sided TNMM margin below the Taiwan interquartile range without supporting comparables.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority may adjust the taxable income to an arm's length amount and impose a surcharge of 100%–200% of the additional tax (per Article 43-2 of the Income Tax Act as reinforced by Transfer Pricing Assessment Rules). If documentation is absent, the same surcharge is doubled; a civil penalty of NT$20,000–NT$200,000 is imposed per missing file.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Transfer pricing aggression does not automatically invoke personal liability unless the director signed confirmations on comparability adjustments that are fraudulent. If the director causes the company to issue a false intercompany conclusion letter with intent to evade tax, he or she becomes directly and personally liable for the surcharge under the 'responsible person of profit-seeking enterprise' doctrine in Article 15 of the Tax Collection Act. Criminal imprisonment of up to 2 years may follow after transfer pricing tax adjustments exceed NT$6 million.
